root_causes: The ambient declaration file `.archgate/rules.d.ts` declares the `RuleSet`, `Severity`, and `GrepMatch` types referenced by all five tracked `.archgate/adrs/ARCH-00x.rules.ts` files (each opens with `/// <reference path="../rules.d.ts" />` and closes with `} satisfies RuleSet;`). archgate's own bundled runtime ships ambient types and so does not need the file at runtime — verified: with `.archgate/rules.d.ts` moved aside, `archgate check` still exits 0 with 5/5 rules passing (file since restored, sha256 534d9e8209b870e29a4679a3d908b6e331010bf21233f2331614c68c59914616). What does need the file on a fresh clone is any TypeScript-aware editor or standalone type-checker resolving the triple-slash references. No CI step runs `tsc`/`bunx tsc`/`tsc --noEmit` or any other TypeScript type-check outside archgate's bundled runtime (verified by grep against .github/workflows/*.y*ml — no hits for `tsc`, `bunx tsc`, `--noEmit`, or `type-check`); the consumer of `.archgate/rules.d.ts` is human-author TypeScript tooling, not CI. Committing the file preserves the type-resolution chain for the five tracked rule files on fresh clones.

The repo's tracked `.gitignore` predates the OMC/OMX directory layout: it only excludes `.omc/state/` and `.omc/sessions/`. The 14+ operational files currently untracked (`.omc/handoffs/*`, `.omc/plans/*`, `.omc/specs/*`, `.omc/project-memory.json`, `.omc/template-version.json`, `.omx/hud-config.json`, `.omx/setup-scope.json`, `.omx/state/update-check.json`) are one `git add -A` away from being committed.
